within_study_findings: Science dissemination videos had higher retention than exercise/problem-solving videos within this channel's analyzed sample
Videos shorter than eight minutes in the sample were associated with stronger retention
Fixed standard introductions were associated with early retention loss
Narration speed showed limited association with retention in reported abstract
studies.warning: Single Spanish-language STEM channel; no randomized video-length assignment, viewer income, all-platform success rate or repeat-person retention.

within_study_findings: Instructional-video group had higher view and share measurements
Practice-test group had higher likes, watch-time duration and average view duration
studies.warning: One channel, sampled videos within pre-existing categories; absolute viewer cohorts, purchase outcomes and all-channel generalization are not established.

within_study_findings: Video duration was not significantly correlated with the selected view, like or comment engagement metrics
Context and mathematical content categories matter; a single length rule did not emerge
studies.warning: Highly viewed selected videos are conditioned on prior visibility, do not include owner retention or actual learning completion, and are not representative of new channels.

comparability_rules: Spanish STEM channel owner-only average view duration and 30-second retention are not equivalent to Turkish public views, likes and comments.
Instructional and practice-test video groups on one Indonesian channel are not independent samples of all learners.
A selected under-eight-minute retention association and a separate null length correlation in Turkish math videos do not contradict each other because samples and outcome metrics differ.
The studies are observational; educational format and video length are selected, not randomly assigned to interchangeable viewer populations.
View events, shares, likes, measured watch minutes and learning outcomes do not reveal an income model, repeat unique viewers or proven educational effectiveness.
Online-course learning-system view statistics from non-YouTube platforms must not be silently pooled with YouTube analytics.
No source supports a universal ideal video duration or causal claim that fixed introductions lower creator revenue.

statistics_search_quality_case.sampling: Four fixed YouTube queries: statistical analysis, data analysis, statistics, statistical methods; top 50 relevance-ranked URLs from each query, cookie-cleared private browsing

manually_rated_quality.rating_system: Global Quality Scale 1-5 and modified DISCERN; two independent subject-expert raters plus adjudicator

limitations: Relevant top-50 search results are selected by YouTube relevance ranking, not a probability sample of all statistics uploads or people.
Only English results were eligible; excludes 22 other-language and 23 off-topic entries as well as 41 duplicates.
Reported 'daily views' is lifetime public views divided by days since upload, not daily longitudinal owner Analytics.
Expert GQS ratings are content-quality judgments under this article's methodology, not demonstrated learning gains or financial returns.
Observational differences in ratings and public engagement have no random assignment; channel audience and exposure are confounded.
This study is different from the three original video-format/retention cohorts and must not be pooled into their sample denominator.
